definition: Punctilious means carefully exact about rules and details of conduct.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word punctilious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know punctilious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The club's punctilious secretary reads the minutes aloud twice — once for content, once for commas.
Careful stops far short of punctilious — careful covers ordinary, everyday attention.
Exacting stops short of punctilious — the exacting demand high standards, while the punctilious honor every fine point of form and etiquette.

Precise means exact in detail generally — a precise measurement, a precise answer — and carries no special interest in manners. Punctilious narrows exactness to conduct: rules, courtesies, ceremony, the fine points of correct form. An engineer can be precise about tolerances yet clueless about which fork the fish course requires; the punctilious never are.

Meticulous means extremely careful and thorough about the details of any task — a meticulous proofreader misses nothing anywhere. Punctilious aims that care specifically at correct form: protocol, etiquette, the proper order of things. A meticulous editor checks every figure; a punctilious diplomat knows which flag outranks which.
